title: Thornleigh Combe
subtitle: A village untouched by tourism. Explore it for yourself.
description: Quietways presents Thornleigh Combe: England as it was, for those who know.

map.alt: An illustrated map of Thornleigh Combe: a High Street of cottages and shops, a green, the church of St Aldhelm, the old school, and fields all round.

card.title: A Scots pine
card.text:
Twenty-two metres, perfectly symmetrical, and evergreen in a way no tree has managed before.

card.text: Space for eight coaches.
Four pairs of brick gateposts in the hedge, a front garden apart. Nos. 1–4 Meadow Cottages, built by the rural district council in 1928, were taken down in 2015 to restore the meadow.

locations.name: The Plough
locations.teaser: A sixteenth-century coaching inn. Sit with the regulars.

card.title: The Locals' Table
card.text: Bookable, £45 for two, includes a half of Combe Bitter and fifteen minutes with the regulars.
Oak beams, adzed by hand: glass-reinforced plastic, Heritage Interiors Ltd, 2016. Guests are asked not to hang coats on them.

card.title: The Plough in earlier days
card.text: Behind the bar: the Plough brand new in 1934, its timbering freshly painted by Hallett's Brewery. Across the road, slate roofs, and Haddow's Garage with two pumps.

image.alt: A 1934 black-and-white photograph of the High Street: the Plough brand new, crisp black timbering on white render and a new tile roof, its sign reading THE PLOUGH, the landlord in the doorway; across the road, slate-roofed cottages and Haddow's Garage with two hand-cranked petrol pumps under glass globes, a 1930s car, a boy with a bicycle on the unmade road.

photos.caption: The Heritage Barn.

photos.alt: Inside the Heritage Barn: a tall plastered room under a boarded pitched ceiling, tall round-arched windows down both sides boarded over from outside, light through the gaps; at the far end one arched window left clear, a visitor looking out of it, and beside it a small empty hymn board; straw bales at left, a cartwheel and a hay rake on the walls, corn dollies on a trestle table at right; pale strips in the floorboards where pews were fixed.
photos.caption: The Heritage Barn, inside.
